title: 1 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Samuel chapter 17 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Samuel Chapter 17.

questions.question: In 1 Samuel 17, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The Philistines gathered their armies at Shochoh
David was sent to bring food to his brothers
Goliath challenged the armies of Israel
Saul and the men of Israel pitched by the valley of Elah
questions.correctAnswer: The Philistines gathered their armies at Shochoh
questions.explanation: The first event in the chapter is the Philistines gathering their armies at Shochoh, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:1.

questions.question: Where did the Philistines gather their armies to battle in 1 Samuel 17?
questions.explanation: The Philistines gathered their armies at Shochoh as stated in 1 Samuel 17:1.

questions.question: Where did Saul and the men of Israel pitch their camp?
questions.explanation: Saul and the men of Israel pitched by the valley of Elah as stated in 1 Samuel 17:2.

questions.question: What separated the armies of the Philistines and Israel in 1 Samuel 17?
questions.explanation: The Philistines stood on one mountain and Israel on another with a valley between them, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:3.

questions.question: What was the name of the Philistine champion who challenged Israel?
questions.explanation: The champion of the Philistines was named Goliath, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:4.

questions.question: How tall was Goliath according to 1 Samuel 17?
questions.explanation: Goliath's height was six cubits and a span, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:4.

questions.question: What was the weight of Goliath's coat of mail?
questions.explanation: The coat of mail weighed five thousand shekels of brass, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:5.

questions.question: What did Goliath have on his legs?
questions.explanation: Goliath wore greaves of brass on his legs, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:6.

questions.question: What was the weight of the head of Goliath's spear?
questions.explanation: The spear's head weighed six hundred shekels of iron, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:7.

questions.question: Who was the youngest son of Jesse mentioned in the chapter?
questions.explanation: David was the youngest son of Jesse, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:14.

questions.question: How many sons did Jesse have according to 1 Samuel 17?
questions.explanation: Jesse had eight sons, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:12.

questions.question: David was sent to bring food to his brothers and to the captain of their thousand.
questions.explanation: Jesse told David to bring food to his brothers and to carry cheese to the captain of their thousand as stated in 1 Samuel 17:17-18.

questions.question: Goliath challenged the armies of Israel to send a man to fight him in single combat.
questions.explanation: Goliath asked the Israelites to choose a man to fight him as stated in 1 Samuel 17:8-10.

questions.question: David was one of the three eldest sons of Jesse who went to battle with Saul.
questions.explanation: David was the youngest son and did not go to battle; the three eldest sons followed Saul as stated in 1 Samuel 17:13-14.

questions.question: The text states that Goliath's spear was the heaviest weapon in the Philistine army.
questions.explanation: The text gives the weight of Goliath's spear head but does not say it was the heaviest weapon in the Philistine army, as seen in 1 Samuel 17:7.

medium.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Samuel Chapter 17 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who was the champion that came out of the camp of the Philistines?
questions.explanation: Goliath is identified as the champion of the Philistines in 1 Samuel 17:23.

questions.question: What will happen to the man who kills Goliath according to 1 Samuel 17:25?
options: He will be enriched with great riches
questions.correctAnswer: He will be enriched with great riches
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:25 states that the king will enrich the man who kills Goliath with great riches.

questions.question: What did David say would be done to the man who kills Goliath?
options: He would be given Saul's armor
He would be given a kingdom
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:25 mentions that the man who kills Goliath will be given the king's daughter.

questions.question: What did David say about Goliath when he spoke to the men around him?
options: He is uncircumcised and defies the armies of the living God
questions.correctAnswer: He is uncircumcised and defies the armies of the living God
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 17:26, David expresses his disdain for Goliath's defiance against Israel and God.

questions.question: What was Eliab's reaction when he heard David speaking?
options: He was angry and questioned David's motives
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry and questioned David's motives
questions.explanation: Eliab's anger was kindled against David as noted in 1 Samuel 17:28.

questions.question: What did David do when Eliab criticized him?
options: He asked what he had done wrong
questions.correctAnswer: He asked what he had done wrong
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 17:29, David responds to Eliab by asking, 'What have I now done? Is there not a cause?'

questions.question: How did Saul react when David offered to fight Goliath?
questions.explanation: Saul expressed doubt about David's ability to fight Goliath, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:33.

questions.question: What past experiences did David mention to convince Saul he could fight Goliath?
options: He had fought in many battles
He had slain a lion and a bear
He was trained by a warrior
questions.correctAnswer: He had slain a lion and a bear
questions.explanation: David mentioned his experiences of killing a lion and a bear to persuade Saul, as noted in 1 Samuel 17:34-35.

questions.question: What did David say about the Lord's role in his past victories?
options: He did it all by himself
The Lord delivered him from danger
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord delivered him from danger
questions.explanation: David stated that the LORD who delivered him from the lion and bear would also deliver him from Goliath, as seen in 1 Samuel 17:37.

questions.question: What armor did Saul put on David before he went to fight Goliath?
questions.explanation: Saul armed David with a coat of mail as mentioned in 1 Samuel 17:38.

questions.question: Why did David refuse to wear Saul's armor?
questions.explanation: David stated he could not go with Saul's armor because he had not proved them, as stated in 1 Samuel 17:39.

questions.question: What did David choose to take with him to fight Goliath?
options: Five smooth stones and a sling
questions.correctAnswer: Five smooth stones and a sling
questions.explanation: David took five smooth stones from the brook and a sling to confront Goliath, as noted in 1 Samuel 17:40.

questions.question: David believed he could defeat Goliath because he had faith in God. Is this statement true?
questions.explanation: David's confidence in facing Goliath stemmed from his faith that the Lord would deliver him, as seen in 1 Samuel 17:37.

questions.question: David was discouraged by the fear of the Israelite soldiers. Is this statement true?
questions.explanation: David was not discouraged by the fear of the soldiers; rather, he was motivated to fight Goliath as he recognized a cause, as seen in 1 Samuel 17:26.

questions.question: Eliab encouraged David to fight Goliath. Is this statement true?
questions.explanation: Eliab actually criticized David and questioned his motives, as noted in 1 Samuel 17:28.

hard.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Samuel Chapter 17.

questions.question: Who came before the Philistine as he approached David?
options: The man that bare the shield
questions.correctAnswer: The man that bare the shield
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'the man that bare the shield went before him' (1 Samuel 17:41), indicating the presence of a shield-bearer in front of Goliath.

questions.question: What did the Philistine think of David when he saw him?
questions.explanation: The Philistine saw David and disdained him because he was just a youth and of a fair countenance (1 Samuel 17:42).

questions.question: What did Goliath call David when he approached him?
questions.explanation: Goliath questioned David, saying, 'Am I a dog, that thou comest to me with staves?' (1 Samuel 17:43), indicating his contempt for David.

questions.question: What did David claim he came in the name of?
questions.explanation: David declared, 'I come to thee in the name of the LORD of hosts, the God of the armies of Israel' (1 Samuel 17:45), emphasizing his reliance on God.

questions.question: What did David predict would happen on that day?
options: The LORD would deliver Goliath into David's hand
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD would deliver Goliath into David's hand
questions.explanation: David stated, 'This day will the LORD deliver thee into mine hand' (1 Samuel 17:46), asserting his faith in God's deliverance.

questions.question: What weapon did David use to slay Goliath?
questions.explanation: David prevailed over Goliath with 'a sling and with a stone' (1 Samuel 17:50), highlighting the unconventional means by which he defeated the giant.

questions.question: What did David do after he killed Goliath?
options: He stood on Goliath and cut off his head
questions.correctAnswer: He stood on Goliath and cut off his head
questions.explanation: The scripture notes that David 'ran, and stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword, and drew it out of the sheath... and cut off his head' (1 Samuel 17:51).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'צְבָאוֹת' (tsabaoth) in 1 Samuel 17:45 mean?
questions.explanation: 'צְבָאוֹת' (tsabaoth) translates to 'armies', referring to God's divine hosts in 1 Samuel 17:45, underscoring David's reliance on divine military power.

questions.question: Which literary technique is used when David speaks about the battle being the LORD's?
questions.explanation: David's statement about the battle being the LORD's exhibits chiasm, as it emphasizes the reversal of human strength versus divine intervention, found in 1 Samuel 17:47.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to David's declaration of God's deliverance in 1 Samuel 17:46?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:31 echoes the theme of divine support, stating 'If God be for us, who can be against us?' which aligns with David's confidence in God's deliverance in 1 Samuel 17:46.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage fulfills the theme of the LORD saving not with sword and spear from 1 Samuel 17:47?
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 1:27 speaks of God choosing the foolish things of the world to confound the wise, reflecting the same theme that God saves without traditional weapons, similar to 1 Samuel 17:47.

questions.question: What comes immediately before David's declaration of faith in 1 Samuel 17:45?
questions.explanation: David's declaration follows Goliath's taunt and challenge to come down to him (1 Samuel 17:44) in the context of their face-off.

questions.question: What does David reference when addressing Saul about his ability to fight Goliath in 1 Samuel 17:34-37?
options: His previous battles with wild animals
questions.correctAnswer: His previous battles with wild animals
questions.explanation: David references his experiences battling a lion and a bear to illustrate his capability and faith, found in 1 Samuel 17:34-36.

questions.question: True or False: David was the youngest son of Jesse.
questions.explanation: The text states that 'David was the youngest' of Jesse's eight sons (1 Samuel 17:14), confirming that he was indeed the youngest.

questions.question: True or False: Goliath was afraid of David when he first saw him.
questions.explanation: Goliath expressed disdain and mocked David, showing he was not afraid but rather contemptuous (1 Samuel 17:42-43).

theological.title: 1 Samuel Chapter 17 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Samuel Chapter 17 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 1 Samuel 17:36 teach about God's providence in sanctification?
options: God's providence protects and empowers the believer against spiritual enemies
Sanctification is achieved through human strength alone
God's providence is limited to physical protection only
Sanctification occurs without any divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence protects and empowers the believer against spiritual enemies
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:36 shows David declaring how God delivered him from the lion and bear, applying this to the coming battle with Goliath, illustrating divine protection and empowerment in sanctification.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and unbelief is highlighted by the reaction of Saul and Israel in 1 Samuel 17:11?
options: Fear and unbelief are natural responses to spiritual warfare but must be overcome by faith
Human sinfulness does not affect responses to God's challenges
Unbelief is irrelevant in God's plan of salvation
Fear is always a sign of personal sin and unforgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Fear and unbelief are natural responses to spiritual warfare but must be overcome by faith
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:11 describes Saul and Israel being dismayed and afraid at Goliath's challenge, illustrating human fear and unbelief that must be confronted by faith in God.

questions.question: What doctrine of salvation is taught in 1 Samuel 17:45 regarding the power to overcome enemies?
options: Salvation and victory come through the name and power of the LORD of hosts, not by human weaponry
Salvation is earned by physical might and weapons
Victory in battle depends solely on human skill
Salvation is unrelated to God's power in earthly conflicts
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation and victory come through the name and power of the LORD of hosts, not by human weaponry
questions.explanation: David's declaration in 1 Samuel 17:45 emphasizes that he comes in the name of the LORD of hosts, teaching that salvation and victory are God's work, not human weapons.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 1 Samuel 17:37 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: In 1 Samuel 17:37, David expresses confidence that the LORD who delivered him from the lion and bear will also deliver him from Goliath, demonstrating God's sovereign control over events.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 1 Samuel 17:47 where David declares the battle belongs to the LORD?
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:47 affirms that the battle belongs to the LORD, reflecting His omnipotence to save and deliver His people.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 17 prepare for the messianic theme of God's anointed king defeating evil?
options: By portraying David as a type of the Messiah who triumphs over enemies by God's power
By focusing solely on military tactics without theological significance
By emphasizing human strength over divine intervention
By rejecting the idea of a future anointed king
questions.correctAnswer: By portraying David as a type of the Messiah who triumphs over enemies by God's power
questions.explanation: The victory of David over Goliath prefigures the messianic king defeating evil through divine power, a theme fulfilled in Christ.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection is made by the theme of God delivering David from wild beasts in 1 Samuel 17:34-35?
options: It symbolizes God's ongoing deliverance through Christ from sin and death
It is only a literal account with no typological meaning
It teaches that human effort is sufficient for salvation
It denies God's involvement in daily protection
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's ongoing deliverance through Christ from sin and death
questions.explanation: David's deliverance from lion and bear foreshadows Christ's ultimate deliverance of believers from sin and death.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Samuel 17:45 and 17:47 teach about God's role in salvation and battle?
options: God alone is the source of salvation and victory; human strength is insufficient
Human weapons are the primary means of salvation
Salvation is unrelated to God's power in battle
Victory depends on alliances rather than divine aid
questions.correctAnswer: God alone is the source of salvation and victory; human strength is insufficient
questions.explanation: Verses 17:45 and 17:47 together affirm that the LORD of hosts is the true source of victory, not sword or spear.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Samuel 17:11 and 17:32 teach about faith versus fear in spiritual conflict?
options: Fear paralyzes God's people, but faith enables bold action against enemies
Fear is righteous and faith is irrelevant
Fear and faith both guarantee victory
questions.correctAnswer: Fear paralyzes God's people, but faith enables bold action against enemies
questions.explanation: Verse 17:11 shows Israel's fear, while 17:32 shows David's faith enabling him to face Goliath, teaching the contrast between fear and faith.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 1 Samuel 17:37 and 17:50 teach about the assurance of God's deliverance?
options: God's deliverance is sure and manifests in the believer's victory over enemies
Deliverance is uncertain and depends on human effort
Victory is accidental with no divine assurance
God delivers only some believers selectively
questions.correctAnswer: God's deliverance is sure and manifests in the believer's victory over enemies
questions.explanation: David's confidence in 17:37 and his actual victory in 17:50 show assurance that God delivers and grants victory.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the story of David and Goliath in 1 Samuel 17:40-51 is merely mythic and teaches reliance on luck rather than God. What does the passage actually teach?
options: David explicitly credits God for his victory and confronts Goliath in the name of the LORD of hosts
David wins through luck and human cleverness alone
The story promotes idol worship of weapons
Victory is attributed to chance and not divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: David explicitly credits God for his victory and confronts Goliath in the name of the LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:45-47 shows David declaring the battle belongs to the LORD, emphasizing divine intervention rather than luck.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's covenant faithfulness is taught in 1 Samuel 17:25 regarding the king's promise to the man who kills Goliath?
options: God's covenant includes the king rewarding godly courage and deliverance of Israel
God's covenant promises are irrelevant to earthly kings
The king acts independently of God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God's covenant includes the king rewarding godly courage and deliverance of Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Samuel 17:25 connects the king's reward to the deliverance of Israel, indicating covenant faithfulness expressed through the king.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in 1 Samuel 17:46 where David proclaims the LORD will deliver Goliath into his hand?
questions.explanation: David's confident proclamation in 1 Samuel 17:46 shows God's powerful ability to deliver enemies into the hands of His servants.

questions.question: What doctrine of sanctification is taught by David rejecting Saul's armor in 1 Samuel 17:39?
options: Sanctification involves reliance on God's provision and personal gifting rather than external worldly means
Sanctification depends on outward appearances and armor
God's grace is unnecessary in sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification involves reliance on God's provision and personal gifting rather than external worldly means
questions.explanation: David's refusal of Saul's armor in 1 Samuel 17:39 shows reliance on what God has equipped him with, teaching sanctification involves dependence on God’s provision.

questions.question: How does 1 Samuel 17:53 connect to the theme of divine vindication and judgment elsewhere in Scripture?
options: The spoiling of the Philistine tents reflects God's judgment on the enemies of His people
Spoiling is purely a military act with no theological meaning
God forbids any judgment on enemies
Divine vindication is unrelated to earthly victories
questions.correctAnswer: The spoiling of the Philistine tents reflects God's judgment on the enemies of His people
questions.explanation: The act described in 1 Samuel 17:53 symbolizes God’s judgment and vindication of Israel against their enemies.
